title: Self-dual $S_3$ gauge theory in 2+1d: lattice model and topological phase transitions
authors: Da-Chuan Lu, Chong Wang, Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract: Electric-magnetic self-duality of the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory, realized microscopically as a half-lattice-translation exchanging electric charge and magnetic flux, has been an influential example of a duality symmetry with an exact lattice realization. We construct the first non-Abelian generalization of this construction: a lattice model of the $S_3$ quantum double $\mathcal{D}(S_3)$ on a tensor product Hilbert space in which the $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{em}}_2$ anyon-permutation symmetry, exchanging the non-Abelian chargeon $C$ and fluxon $F$, is realized via lattice translation. Consequently we find that the zigzag boundary termination of the model realizes, without fine-tuning, a gapless critical edge state described by the tetracritical Ising CFT. The bulk admits three independent $\mathbb{Z}_2^{\mathrm{em}}$-preserving bosonic perturbations, driving $\mathcal{D}(S_3)$ into distinct gapped phases. We analyze these transitions by three independent methods: category-theoretic anyon condensation, microscopic lattice Hamiltonians, and Chern-Simons-Higgs theory, which all agree, yielding a unified picture. These examples motivate a minimal-condensation principle: proliferating a bosonic anyon generically drives condensation of a minimal condensable algebra containing it, with symmetry-related condensates appearing as degenerate vacua that spontaneously break the anyon-permutation symmetry. Our model construction extends to an infinite family of self-dual dihedral quantum doubles $\mathcal{D}(D_{2n})$. Notably, each model is sign-problem-free, opening the door to large-scale numerical exploration of the phases of non-Abelian Chern-Simons-Higgs theories.
summary: This paper constructs and analyzes a lattice model for the $S_3$ quantum double gauge theory, generalizing known self-dual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ systems. By employing three independent theoretical methods, the authors map out the phase diagram, predicting critical edge states described by the Ising CFT and identifying multiple distinct gapped phases in the bulk.
main_problem: The research aims to generalize the concept of electric-magnetic self-duality from $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theories to non-Abelian systems, specifically analyzing phase transitions in $S_3$ quantum double models.
main_result: The model exhibits a gapless critical edge state described by the tetracritical Ising CFT, and the bulk undergoes three independent gapped phase transitions driven by bosonic perturbations.
method: The authors employ multiple complementary theoretical approaches: category-theoretic anyon condensation, microscopic lattice Hamiltonians analysis, and Chern-Simons-Higgs (CSH) theory to characterize the phase diagram.
model_or_system: The system is a lattice model for the $S_3$ quantum double $\mathcal{D}(S_3)$ on a tensor product Hilbert space. It generalizes the self-dual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory and is constructed to be sign-problem-free.
key_observables: The existence of gapless critical edge states, the nature of the three distinct gapped phases in the bulk, and the realization of the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ anyon-permutation symmetry.
important_parameters: Coupling constants ($\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3$) governing bosonic perturbations; lattice size for numerical checks.
main_assumptions: The proposal introduces a 'minimal-condensation principle,' assuming that proliferating a bosonic anyon generically drives condensation of a minimal condensable algebra.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the phase diagram for $D(S_3)$ and its dependence on three perturbation parameters $(\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3)$. Table I details critical boundaries and neighboring gapped phases.
paper_structure: The paper develops a unified picture by analyzing transitions using three independent methods (anyon condensation, lattice Hamiltonians, CSH theory). It establishes the minimal-condensation principle and extends the model to infinite families of dihedral quantum doubles $\mathcal{D}(D_{2n})$.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding how topological order breaks down in non-Abelian gauge theories, connecting lattice models directly to continuum CFT descriptions.
